Hi everyone! I'm Kavindya Jayathilaka, goes by Kivi. I'm excited to get to know you all!

I'll be joining the PhD program in Operations Research at SMU this upcoming fall. I graduated from UTK with an Mathter's in Mathematics. During my master's, I worked on a project with one of my professors to learn and explore the Lean programming language. While learning Lean 4 and proving theorems, I became increasingly interested in contributing formalized theorems in Numerical Analysis.

I haven't come across much content related to Linear Algebra or Numerical Analysis yet, so I was wondering whether there are already theorem libraries or ongoing projects in those areas. If so, who would be the best person to reach out to for more information?

Looking forward to connecting with everyone!

Hi Kivi! I don't know anything about Numerical Analysis, but what kind of results are you looking for in Linear Algebra? You're certainly aware that Mathlib contains a lot of definitions in this area...

Filippo A. E. Nuccio said:

Hi Kivi! I don't know anything about Numerical Analysis, but what kind of results are you looking for in Linear Algebra? You're certainly aware that Mathlib contains a lot of definitions in this area...

I imagine it was meant as Numerical Linear Algebra. @Kavindya Jayathilaka you can look at SciLean by @Tomas Skrivan. I understand development on it has stopped, but it is still probably the most relevant project I know of. You can look also at TorchLean which has API for tensor operations and floating point (it's meant for neural networks though).

Maybe the main question is whether you want to formalize just the general theory, or work on runnable algorithms. For the first part, for example we do have numerical analysis relevant results about orthogonal families of polynomials (eg: docs#Polynomial.Chebyshev.T, docs#Lagrange.interpolate) and you could look at docs#trapezoidal_error_le for an example of a quadrature rule and error bound. People wise, the main authors of each mathlib file are listed at the top, so that can help you find who to talk to.
Oh and if you search on Zulip, there has been a bunch of work on the SVD, but I'm not up to date.

Yeah SciLean is pretty much dead right now but I started extracting the parts that deal with multidimensional arrays and properly formalizing everything along the way. You should be able to write executable programs which are parametrized over the main real number type. Prove properties with real numbers, execute with Float, connect floats with real numbers using interval arithmetics.

https://github.com/lecopivo/NumLean as the name suggests it tries to by NumPy but in Lean and fully formalized.

The main result right now is the linear isometry between the tensor type and Euclidean space https://github.com/lecopivo/NumLean/blob/89d65bfb3e43ee290ba88ff915c961c798f440af/NumLean/Data/Tensor/Algebra/Lawful.lean#L251

Here is a quick start for NumPy users https://lecopivo.github.io/NumLeanManual/Quickstart-for-NumPy-Users/The-Basics/#NumLean-Manual--Quickstart-for-NumPy-Users--The-Basics

I haven't announced the project yet as I still need to write a section on how to prove things and a section on general structure of the project. However, if NumLean would be useful to you then please get in touch, tell me how you would like to use it and I can prioritize its development.

It would be really useful to know in more detail what you would like to do. If you are interested only in proofs or do you also want to run the verified algorithms. NumLean is going to be useful only in the later case.

As for numerical analysis, Mathlib only has two types of matrix norms I think (Frobenius and sup) with not a lot of content on them, I don't think there's anything about rates of convergence, and Newton-Raphson exists but has almost no results.

Perhaps a good way to start would be to define rate of convergence and prove basic results about it, such as that Newton-Raphson converges with a quadratic rate for simple roots.
^^ I second this, I would love to get some numerical analysis / numerical linear algebra results into Mathlib.

Thank you so much for the information. I will look in to those. I originally wanted to prove the existence and uniqueness of SVD. However I realize that there are some lack of theorems which I need. Perhaps I should start with basic theorems such as SPD or matrix norms.
See #Is there code for X? > Singular Value Decomposition
